XenotypeDef.label: Kitul
XenotypeDef.description: Kitul are the result of early experimentation into xenogenetics. They are athletic and retain superficial animal characteristics, with keen senses and excellent eyesight. Kitul are competent with ranged weaponry and function well in cold weather.\n\nDue to their relatively early introduction in human history, Kitul have been subjected to generations of discrimination. Their superior reflexes and combat potential lead many Kitul to be pressed into service as soldiers or mercenaries and their pleasing appearances makes them targets for the wealthy and powerful. While groups of Kitul have found acceptance on certain glitterworlds, many have retreated into isolated and insular communities on other planets. A significant number have made their way into piracy, and kitul raiders are not an uncommon sight on rimworlds.
XenotypeDef.descriptionShort: Kitul are the result of early experimentation into xenogenetics. They are athletic and retain superficial animal characteristics, with keen senses and excellent eyesight.

XenotypeDef.label: Artemid
XenotypeDef.description:
Artemids were designed to be a greater part of nature than a natural human ever could be. Brightly colored and possessing a tail and acid-spitting glands, this xenotype thrives while working with plants and animals. They can freely ingest certain plant-based drugs.

Independent Artemid communities are rare, but the presence of even one Artemid can greatly aid a struggling farm, so they are often welcomed with open arms by those that need them. Elsewehere, they have a reputation for being foppish and vain, and a common stereotype is that Artemids are second sons of nobility or dissatisfied rich children who sought an escape from their lives.

Some industrial planets actively and aggressively trade in Artemid xenotypes, implanting the genes into any worker willing to take them. When properly managed, food exports can be drastically increased, though the Artemids' fragile mental state must be carefully managed.

XenotypeDef.label: Nizhar
XenotypeDef.description: Created to be a peak physical combatant, Nizhar are highly capable in melee combat and grow tired less quickly than most. These abilities come with a great detriment to many of their other skills, and they grow restless when they are unable to kill. Their extreme metabolic needs render them completely sterile and dependent on wake-up.\n\nNizhar are sometimes deployed alongside hussars in combat, but they are competent as stiletto killers, front-line berserkers, and anything in-between. In stark contrast to the closely-related Hussar xenotype, Nizhar are fully capable of blending in with baseliner populations, so many career assassins willingly become Nizhar. The xenotype is banned on many worlds due to the lack of outward signs of their genetic modifications.

Their extreme metabolic needs render them completely sterile and dependent on wake-up.

XenotypeDef.label: Prole
XenotypeDef.description:
Bred to create the ultimate worker drone, proles are easygoing and dependable. They tend to be skilled at many necessary industrial tasks and are genetically immune to certain stimulants. While they are competent at combat, they recover slowly and are somewhat prone to disease and infection.

Proles are not the result of genuine curiosity in pushing human limits or populating dead worlds. They were engineered by corporate interests seeking more efficient workers. Inspection of their genetics reveal sloppy work, leaving Proles with shorter lifespans and weaker immune systems than baseliners. Prole communities tend to thrive even on resource-depleted planets long-abandoned by their corporate masters. The average prole does not lament their position in life - perhaps an intentional result of their genetics. 

Many Proles retain the tradition of being named after the worker designations of their ancestors, though not all remember this practice. Those named traditionally tend to nickname themselves to preserve individuality.

They tend to be skilled at many necessary industrial tasks and are genetically immune to certain stimulants. While they are competent at combat, they recover slowly and are somewhat prone to disease and infection.

XenotypeDef.label: gwennin
XenotypeDef.description: Friendly, dog-like xenohumans with strong stomachs, the gwennin are commonly found among yttakin settlements. Unlike the yttakin, Gwennin are far more likely to engage in productive diplomacy with other xenotypes. Gwennin are very social and easy to please, though they are somewhat unimaginative. Their straightforward and optimistic mental states leave Gwennin less susceptible to psychic interference.\n\nWhile not every yttakin settlement enjoys the presence of gwennin, they are tolerated due to their ability to act as a bridge between furskinned and non-furskinned societies. Being smaller and meeker than their yttakin allies, the gwennin often find themselves in subservient roles - not that they particularly mind.

XenotypeDef.label: reaper
XenotypeDef.description: Reapers are medical specialists engineered to fulfill a specific role - to hold back the tides of death. Designed to keep tending to people even in hopeless situations, reapers make for excellent doctors and surgeons, but they are utterly incapable of violence.\n\nThe reaper's distinctive horn was designed to differentiate them from soldiers on the battlefield. They can extinguish fires using foam sprayed from special glands in their necks, and they can keep themselves calm and collected even when placed under incredible stress. Reapers originated on the conflict-prone glitterworld Rogia, though some variants from other worlds have been retromodded to be able to fight on the front lines, or retain a similar appearance to baseliners.
